To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

random sampling of UniRef100 sequences is an effective approach for generating a reference database of protein sequence for protein-RNA interface predictions and that the FastRNABind online server is the only protein interface prediction server that accepts hundreds of protein sequence per submission and requires the user to generate PSSM profiles.

(1) Random sampling of UniRef100 sequences produces better PSSM-based encoding of protein sequences than using the entire UniProt database, (2) The accuracy of protein-RNA residue binding predictors can be improved by sampling a representative subset of the entire UniRef database and (3) The sampling procedure described in this paper can be used for improving the practical utility of other protein-protein and DNA-protein interface predictors.

In summary, our research is concerned with
improving the accuracy of protein-RNA residue interaction prediction by using PSSM encoding of protein sequences.
the development of a fast and accurate protein-RNA interface predictor.
the development of a practical, fast and accurate tool for predicting protein-Rna interfaces that can handle a large number of protein queries.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
FastRNABindr, the new and improved version of RNAbindR, is an accurate, fast and practical online tool for predicting the interface residues of proteins in protein-RNA complexes.

FastRNABind is an improved version of the RNABindR predictor that uses a random sampling approach for determining an appropriate reference database of protein amino acid sequences for predicting the interface residues in a protein-RNA complex.
our work has led to the development of a novel protein-RNA interface predictor, which is faster and more accurate than the state-of-the art protein-RNA interface predictions servers.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the random sampling approach for determining the reference database for a protein sequence based predictor is superior to the sequence similarity reduction approach.
FastRNABindr is an accurate and fast protein-RNA interface predictor that can be used for large scale prediction of protein-RNA interactions.
FastRNABind is the fastest and the most accurate protein-RNA interface predictor that is available as a public online service.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the performance of a protein-protein and/or protein-DNA interface residue predictor can be improved by using a representative subset of the UniRef database instead of the entire UniRef database.

random sampling of the protein sequences in UniProt can be used to generate representative databases that can be used to improve the practical utility of sequence-based protein-protein and other protein-ligand interface residue prediction tools.
the quality of a protein-RNA binding site predictor is not directly correlated to the size of the protein sequence database that is used to generate PSSM profiles.
